names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 19 aprilie, «Sfântul Ierarh Gheorghe Mărturisitorul, Episcopul Antiohiei Pisidiei».

Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Απριλίου, «Όσιος Γεώργιος ο Ομολογητής Επίσκοπος Πισιδίας», with the rank word, the epithet and the see left off; the life page heads him «Οσιος Γεωργιος ο Ομολογητης, Επισκοπος Πισιδιας».

floruit.note: The page fixes one end and bounds the other: he resisted the iconoclast council «at the council of 754», and was exiled by «the emperor Constantine V, called Copronymus, whose reign the page dates 741 to 775», dying in exile. So he was alive in 754 and dead by 775; no year of repose is printed.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (20 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 19 aprilie — «Sfântul Ierarh Gheorghe Mărturisitorul, Episcopul Antiohiei Pisidiei»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Απριλίου — «Όσιος Γεώργιος ο Ομολογητής Επίσκοπος Πισιδίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him. Its account is plainly the same man's — a bishop in Pisidia who was summoned with the other bishops to Constantinople in the iconoclast years, stood against the abolition of the icons, was exiled and died in exile, and was called Confessor for it — and it adds three things the Romanian page withheld: that the council he was called to was that of 754, that the emperor who exiled him was Constantine V Copronymus, whose reign it dates 741 to 775, and that he was made bishop «Πισιδίας», of Pisidia, where doxologia.ro says «Antiohiei Pisidiei», of Antioch in Pisidia. It gives no year of his birth or death, so no `dates` were taken; the 754 of the council and the 741–775 of the reign are the page's dates for those events and not for him. The page prints no hymn and no relic.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (20 September 2026).
